baseline_prompt_en: A Clockpunk travel photograph of a fictional woman, her face and hair appearance guided by the supplied portrait, attending practical clockwork in use at a canal departure pavilion before sunrise. Give her the portrait's softly tapered face, dark eyes, natural lip shape and short dark bob with fine separated fringe. The portrait guides these visible appearance cues; the attendant and her circumstances are invented for this scene. Her intent concentration, the gentle light on her cheek and the relaxed open neck of her cream linen shirt give her presence a quiet, natural appeal. A fitted dark green waistcoat and plain linen skirt belong to the canal city's preindustrial material world. She stands to the left of a waist-high oak departure table, watching a small brass boat marker on its inclined route board. The first passenger boat is drawing level with the landing beyond her, so the machine and the real journey occupy the same moment. She has just removed the square-ended winding key, holding it loosely in her lowered right hand beside her hip, while her left palm rests on the outer oak frame. Both arms stay on her side of the machine and her face turns toward its marker. Make the machine's connected working structure large and clear. A pear-shaped iron weight hangs freely beneath a cord wound around an exposed drive drum. The drum shaft carries a toothed wheel meshing with a second wheel and a smaller terminal pinion. The terminal pinion engages a horizontal toothed rack fixed to the boat-marker carriage, which runs directly beneath the engraved route line. An escapement wheel contacts a pallet on a lever visibly linked to a slender pendulum in the lower right corner of this same open frame. The suspended weight, drum, touching gear teeth and marker rack are visible together across the open front, with real spacing between moving parts. This is useful, hand-built infrastructure in oak, iron and brass; each working surface shows modest wear from use. Frame her from mid-thigh upward beside the entire table and its hanging weight in a landscape photograph. Look across the pavilion at a slight angle that reveals the inclined board and the front transmission together. Keep her face and the machine clear within one shared plane of attention, with the approaching boat readable between the stone columns behind them. Cool predawn canal light enters the open side, and a small warm oil lamp models her cheek and the teeth of the gears. Restrained photographic color, credible skin texture, hand-filed metal edges and soft water reflections make the fictional mechanism feel physically present.
